author: sooner state news
title: Phone scams continue to target potential victims in Tulsa County
text:
Phone scams are continuing to target residents in Tulsa County, according to a May 6 announcement. Scammers are using publicly available information online to find family members of inmates at the Tulsa County Jail and then attempt to obtain money from them over the phone.
The issue is significant because these scams prey on people concerned for their loved ones, often leading victims to lose substantial amounts of money. The scammers claim they can secure an inmate’s release if a bond or payment for an ankle monitor is made over the phone.
Officials report that the Tulsa County Jail has received calls from individuals who say someone claiming to be a bondsman asked for payment by phone. “If your loved one is currently in the Tulsa County Jail and you receive one of these calls, hang up. IT’S A SCAM!” said officials in their statement.
Authorities remind residents that only inmates or their families should contact bond companies directly, not the other way around. To post bond, either a family member or a bondsman must go in person to the jail’s bonds and release window; payments are not handled over the phone. They also warn that if someone insists you stay on the line or tells you not to hang up, it is another sign of a scam.
Another version of this scam involves callers telling people they have an arrest warrant for missing federal grand jury duty and demanding immediate payment—sometimes through cash cards, cash apps, or cryptocurrency purchased at Bitcoin kiosks—to avoid arrest by law enforcement.
The Tulsa County Sheriff’s Office provides law enforcement services including detention and court security throughout Tulsa County and employs more than 600 personnel according to the official website . Vic Regalado serves as sheriff of the agency according to the official website .
summary: Scammers are using publicly available information online to find family members of inmates at the Tulsa County Jail and then attempt to obtain money from them over the phone. The issue is significant because these scams prey on people concerned for their loved ones, often leading victims to lose substantial amounts of money. The scammers claim they can secure an inmate’s release if a bond or payment for an ankle monitor is made over the phone.
